articles.title: Residential Steel Framing: A Guide for General Contractors
articles.audience: General contractors and custom-home builders
articles.purpose: Decide whether adding project-specific residential steel framing is a suitable option for the GC’s work.
articles.practicalOutput: A concise adoption overview and project-fit summary describing Wheeler supply, builder-crew assembly, crew preparation and design-team involvement.
articles.scope: Residential project fit; substantiated material advantages; Wheeler’s supply and on-site assembly model; overview of responsibilities and the adoption sequence. Copy revision priority: improve natural flow, concrete examples and the explanation of Wheeler’s value. Retain the approved topic, FAQ and further reading.

articles.title: How to Compare Custom-Home Steel Framing Quotes in Southern California
articles.audience: Homeowners and builders comparing proposals
articles.purpose: Normalize two or more actual framing proposals for the same approved home design.
articles.practicalOutput: A side-by-side worksheet with rows for engineering/coordination, supply/preparation, transport, installation, wall-performance scope, quoted amount, excluded work and comparable adjusted total.
articles.scope: Record the same design and estimate date; align included scope and responsibilities; enter separately quoted missing work; compare equivalent totals; identify unresolved financial inputs. Copy revision priority: improve the copy and incorporate Stacie’s SME review, especially the service description and quote-comparison guidance. Retain the approved topic.

articles.title: Wood to Cold-Formed Steel Framing: Preparing Your Crew
articles.audience: GCs and framing crews transitioning from wood
articles.purpose: Prepare a wood-framing crew to understand the material-specific knowledge required for cold-formed steel.
articles.practicalOutput: A learning matrix: transferable skill, material-specific difference, preparation or education needed, and the responsible source of approved project information.
articles.scope: Plan reading and layout skills; specified-system equipment and handling awareness; structural framing versus partitions; current industry education; limits of crew decisions and communication with the design team.

articles.title: Steel vs. Wood vs. Concrete: Comparing Installation Costs
articles.audience: Owners and builders comparing framing materials
articles.purpose: Compare equivalent residential installation costs across wood, cold-formed steel and a clearly identified concrete system.
articles.practicalOutput: A cost-category comparison table identifying the structural system, equivalent project scope, included work and supported cost inputs for each alternative.
articles.scope: Identify the concrete system being discussed. Compare equivalent residential structural scopes and explain supported cost categories. Do not invent estimates, combine non-equivalent scopes or name a universal cheapest option.

articles.title: Custom Steel Framing vs. Panelized and Modular Homes in Los Angeles
articles.audience: Custom-home owners, architects and builders evaluating delivery models
articles.purpose: Explain the differences between material, off-site preparation and whole-home delivery methods.
articles.practicalOutput: A delivery-method comparison matrix distinguishing framing material, off-site preparation, preassembled panels and volumetric modules; compare customization, scope and logistics without treating these categories as mutually exclusive.
articles.scope: Definitions and overlaps; customization and repetition; supplier scope; factory quality checks; total schedule and logistics; Wheeler’s custom supply and complementary panelized work.

articles.title: Steel vs. Wood Framing for a Wildfire Rebuild
articles.audience: Southern California homeowners rebuilding after wildfire
articles.purpose: Explain the material and planning factors that shape a rebuild framing decision.
articles.practicalOutput: A homeowner material-decision worksheet comparing noncombustibility, material behavior, crew readiness, engineered scope and budget inputs for the actual rebuild.
articles.scope: Combustibility and moisture behavior; complete-home resilience; project budget and crew readiness; approved design and framing scope; connection to existing local rebuild pages.

articles.title: Planning Your First Residential Steel-Framing Project
articles.audience: GCs planning their first residential steel job
articles.purpose: Give general contractors a high-level overview of the coordination needed before their first residential steel-framing project.
articles.practicalOutput: An approachable planning overview covering early coordination, project information, broad delivery considerations and the installation team.
articles.scope: Keep this explicitly high-level. Remove detailed site-readiness procedures and proprietary operational methods. Obtain Wheeler’s accuracy review before publication; do not provide installation instructions or reveal Wheeler’s IP.

articles.title: How a Custom-Home Steel Framing Project Comes Together
articles.audience: Architects, engineers and custom-home builders
articles.purpose: Explain Wheeler’s customer process through an inviting, plain-language walkthrough.
articles.practicalOutput: A verified walkthrough of the main stages, customer expectations and collaboration between Wheeler, the architect, engineer and builder.
articles.scope: Obtain Wheeler’s answers before drafting. Replace the responsibility matrix with a digestible process narrative. Use a confirmed, approved project example where available and keep private process details out of the article.
questionsForWheeler: Who usually contacts Wheeler first, and when should they involve you?
What information do you need at the first conversation?
What happens between that conversation and a proposal?
How do you collaborate with the architect, engineer, and builder?
What are the main milestones before framing delivery?

What decisions or misunderstandings commonly need clarification?

Which process details can be public, and which should remain private?

articles.title: Qualifying for California Wildfire Insurance Discounts
articles.audience: Homeowners budgeting wildfire insurance
articles.purpose: Help homeowners understand available wildfire-insurance programs and how to pursue qualification.
articles.practicalOutput: A qualification guide covering eligibility, recognized mitigation measures, documentation and the steps homeowners take with the relevant program or insurer.
articles.scope: Make program qualification the main task and calculations secondary. Verify current program requirements before publication. Distinguish insurer-specific conditions from IBHS designation; keep actual quote comparison in November 18.

articles.title: Steel Framing and Wildfire Resilience: A Rebuild Planning Checklist
articles.audience: Homeowners rebuilding in wildfire-exposed communities
articles.purpose: Record the whole-home resilience decisions and evidence a homeowner’s rebuild team must coordinate alongside the steel framing.
articles.practicalOutput: A rebuild planning checklist with rows for roof, exterior-wall covering, openings, vents, property surroundings and maintenance; identify the decision, responsible role and project-specific evidence without supplying assembly recipes.
articles.scope: Briefly define the contribution of noncombustible framing; organize whole-home design and maintenance decisions in a usable checklist; record applicable design/evidence and professional responsibility; connect to existing Wheeler fire-resilience and local rebuild pages.

articles.title: Steel Framing for Custom Homes
articles.audience: Architects and builders designing open-plan homes
articles.purpose: Explain how a custom home’s layout, openings, service routes and finishes are coordinated with project-specific steel framing.
articles.practicalOutput: A design-focused overview of layout and trade coordination, with open-plan layouts as one example.
articles.scope: Retain the original design focus while broadening the framing from open-plan homes to custom homes. Avoid repeating the general GC introduction or Wheeler’s customer-process walkthrough. Do not promise spans or provide structural design instructions.

articles.title: Selecting a Supplier to Frame Your Los Angeles Custom Home
articles.audience: Custom-home owners and builders preparing a supplier shortlist
articles.purpose: Help custom-home owners and builders evaluate a framing supplier’s suitability for their project.
articles.practicalOutput: A supplier-selection guide covering scope, customization, relevant experience, design-team coordination, delivery and installation responsibility.
articles.scope: Adopt Stacie’s title. Explain Wheeler’s approach accurately. Keep the focus on supplier fit rather than document verification, detailed quotation comparison or a repeated delivery-model comparison.

articles.title: Steel Framing, Fire-Rated Assemblies and Type II Construction
articles.audience: Architects, engineers and builders evaluating fire performance
articles.purpose: Clearly distinguish the three performance and classification concepts.
articles.practicalOutput: A clear three-concept comparison: noncombustible material, the tested/approved complete assembly and whole-building Type II classification, with the scope and responsible evaluator for each.
articles.scope: Material combustibility; complete assembly ratings; construction classification; steel with combustible adjacent products; professional approval; evidence scope.

articles.title: How Fire-Resistive Home Construction Can Affect Insurance Costs
articles.audience: Homeowners evaluating insurance for a new home or wildfire rebuild
articles.purpose: Explain how complete-home construction, documented resilience measures and insurer-recognized classifications can affect homeowners’ insurance costs.
articles.practicalOutput: A homeowner guide connecting construction features, supporting documentation and insurer assessment, with a clear explanation of Wheeler’s contribution within the complete home.
articles.scope: Homeowners’ insurance rather than construction-period builders’ risk. Explain construction-related underwriting factors and potential premium benefits using current, supported information. Steel framing alone does not establish a discount, coverage eligibility or whole-home classification. Keep program qualification, the IBHS application and actual quote comparison in their separate articles.

articles.title: Wood vs. Steel Framing: Comparing Long-Term Ownership Costs
articles.audience: Owners evaluating costs after occupancy
articles.purpose: Explain initial and ongoing ownership-cost categories and the assumptions needed for a useful comparison.
articles.practicalOutput: A transparent ownership-cost worksheet using supported figures or clearly identified homeowner inputs.
articles.scope: Separate initial and ongoing costs. Record the source, date and assumptions for each input. Do not invent maintenance or insurance savings; keep material behavior and actual insurance quotation comparison in their separate articles.

articles.title: IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home: Requirements and Designation
articles.audience: Rebuilding homeowners pursuing a property designation
articles.purpose: Explain the requirements and process for this specific whole-property designation.
articles.practicalOutput: A designation roadmap covering requirements, application, evaluation and ongoing obligations.
articles.scope: Use current program information. Distinguish this designation from insurer-specific discount eligibility and avoid repeating the October 22 qualification overview.

articles.title: Steel Framing for Complex Roofs: A Design Coordination Guide
articles.audience: Architects and builders designing complex residential roofs
articles.purpose: Explain coordination of roof geometry, room volumes, services and finishes at design level.
articles.practicalOutput: A roof-design coordination guide covering the information shared by the architect, engineer, builder and framing supplier.
articles.scope: Keep this at overall design level. Do not include component fabrication, connection details or structural prescriptions; retain the distinct roof-design intent.

articles.title: Who Does What on a Wildfire Rebuild?
articles.audience: Homeowners assembling a rebuild team

articles.practicalOutput: An approachable explanation of who contributes what at each rebuild stage.
articles.scope: Keep the roles clear and homeowner-friendly. Do not imply Wheeler provides installation or professional engineering services without confirmed scope. Avoid duplicating the customer-process walkthrough or professional document guidance.

articles.title: Wood vs. Steel Framing: How Material Movement Affects Finishes
articles.audience: General contractors and custom-home builders coordinating material selection and finished surfaces
articles.purpose: Explain framing-material behavior and its relevance to finished surfaces.
articles.practicalOutput: A material-behavior comparison with high-level finish-coordination considerations.
articles.scope: Avoid universal claims about cracking, settling or maintenance. Keep costs and insurance calculations in the financial articles and exclude proprietary methods or fabrication details.

articles.title: Understanding Steel Framing Quotes: Allowances, Exclusions and Changes

articles.title: Steel-Framed Homes: Understanding Fire and Building Code Documents

articles.purpose: Explain what relevant documents establish and who provides or reviews them.
articles.practicalOutput: A guide matching relevant documentation to its purpose, provider and reviewer.

articles.title: Steel Framing for Hillside Homes: Access and Delivery Planning
articles.audience: Architects and builders planning constrained hillside residential sites
articles.purpose: Explain high-level access and delivery considerations for constrained hillside residential sites.
articles.practicalOutput: A general overview of early access, delivery and project coordination considerations.
articles.scope: Keep this high-level to protect Wheeler’s site-readiness IP. Exclude foundation work, anchoring, detailed handling procedures and proprietary operational methods.

articles.title: Planning Curves and Custom Architectural Features with Steel Framing
articles.audience: Architects developing unusual residential geometry
articles.purpose: Discuss overall architectural possibilities and the design coordination needed to evaluate them.
articles.practicalOutput: An architectural overview of curves and custom features using overall project examples and approved design information.
articles.scope: Exclude bendable-track techniques, fabrication details and component-level demonstrations. Keep complex roof coordination in the separate roof article.

articles.title: Comparing Home Insurance Quotes for Steel and Wood Framed Homes
articles.audience: Homeowners comparing written insurance quotations for the same property
articles.purpose: Help homeowners compare actual insurance offers on equivalent terms and identify differences in coverage, deductibles and total cost.
articles.practicalOutput: A side-by-side policy comparison worksheet recording reconstruction value, coverage limits, deductibles, exclusions, premium, quotation date and assumptions still to confirm with the insurer.

Match property and coverage assumptions, identify remaining differences and distinguish total premium from a wildfire-related component. This is a practical quote-comparison task; do not repeat October 30’s construction-and-underwriting explanation, program eligibility guidance or designation requirements. Do not invent prices or promise steel-only savings.

articles.title: Steel-Framed Exterior Walls: Fire, Moisture and Thermal Performance
articles.audience: Architects and builders coordinating the building envelope
articles.purpose: Explain whole-wall performance at a general design level.
articles.practicalOutput: A high-level explanation of fire, moisture and thermal performance within the complete exterior wall.
articles.scope: Avoid assembly recipes, fastening schedules and component dimensions. Explain coordinated whole-wall performance without promising outcomes from framing alone.
